documents.source_category: Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: Bogala Graphite Lanka PLC is a single standalone entity (subsidiary of Graphit Kropfmuhl GmbH, 86.46% owner) with no subsidiaries of its own -- the filing presents one set of statements, not separate Group/Company columns, so basis is recorded as GROUP by convention (the entity's full results). FYE is 31 December (calendar year), so this quarter (ended 30/06/2026) is Q2 FY2026, not Q1 -- confirmed via the balance sheet comparative date (31 December 2025, the prior FYE) and the Statement of Changes in Equity opening balance date (1 January 2026). The filing presents BOTH a 'Quarter ended 30th June' column (3-month, used throughout this entry) and a 'Period ended 30th June' column (6-month cumulative, Jan-Jun) side by side -- the printed 'Variance' column in the P&L (e.g. Revenue 14.8%) is computed against the 6-MONTH cumulative figures, NOT the 3-month quarter figures used here, so it was not used directly; all % changes in this entry/note were independently recomputed from the quarterly (3-month) current vs prior-year figures. Those quarterly figures were verified internally consistent: Revenue - Cost of Sales = Gross Profit exactly in both years; Gross Profit + Other Income + Net Exchange Gain - Admin - Selling&Distribution = Profit from Operation (165,706 for 2026, 102,339 for 2025, both tie); Profit from Operation + Finance Income - Finance Expenses = PBT exactly (168,372 and 110,216); PBT - Tax = PAT (within LKR '000 rounding); and EPS = PAT / 94,632,904 shares in issue recomputes to 0.93 (2026) and 0.81 (2025), matching the printed EPS exactly -- no column-swap or dual-rendering ambiguity was found. Balance sheet: no comparative balance sheet as at 30/06/2025 is provided in this filing (only current quarter vs FYE 31/12/2025), which is normal CSE quarterly-filing practice -- so no true YoY balance-sheet comparison is possible from this document alone; only the current-quarter balance-sheet figures are stored. short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings are both 0 -- the Company discloses no interest-bearing bank borrowings in either the non-current or current liabilities sections (only provisions, employee benefits, deferred tax, trade/other payables and current taxation). capex = acquisition of PP&E (47,858) + acquisition of intangible assets (2,690).

interim_updates.note_text: Bogala Graphite Lanka PLC reported Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended 30 June 2026; FYE 31 December) revenue of Rs.520.0mn, up 17.1% YoY from Rs.443.9mn, with gross profit up a stronger 41.8% to Rs.251.1mn (from Rs.177.1mn) as gross margin expanded from 39.9% to 48.3% of revenue -- i.e. unit economics improved, not just volume/price. Profit from Operation rose 61.9% to Rs.165.7mn (from Rs.102.3mn), helped by administrative expenses falling 6.7% to Rs.44.3mn, though selling and distribution expenses rose 10.5% to Rs.66.6mn (from Rs.60.3mn) for the quarter, a partial offset. Note 7 discloses the Company's net exchange gain (included within operating profit) fell to Rs.23.7mn for the quarter's cumulative period from Rs.52.8mn prior year -- for the quarter alone this line was Rs.25.0mn (2026) vs Rs.35.0mn (2025), a 28.6% YoY decline in this currency-translation tailwind that partially offset the improvement in trading margin. PBT rose 52.8% to Rs.168.4mn (from Rs.110.2mn), but income tax expense rose far faster, up 139.2% to Rs.80.3mn (from Rs.33.6mn) -- the effective tax rate jumped to 47.7% of PBT from 30.5% a year earlier. As a result PAT grew only 14.9% to Rs.88.1mn (from Rs.76.6mn), and net margin actually contracted slightly to 16.9% (from 17.3%) even as gross and operating margins both expanded materially -- the tax-rate increase, not operating performance, is what capped bottom-line growth this quarter. No segmental note is presented (Bogala is a single-product graphite miner/processor). Balance sheet at 30/06/2026 (vs FYE 31/12/2025, no 30/06/2025 comparative provided in this filing): total assets grew to Rs.1,897.8mn (from Rs.1,693.3mn at FYE), cash and cash equivalents rose to Rs.508.2mn (from Rs.343.2mn), and the Company carries zero interest-bearing borrowings on either side of the balance sheet. Net assets per share was Rs.16.19, though this is actually DOWN from Rs.20.97 a year earlier per the filing's own Note 12.2 -- the decline reflects a large prior-year cash balance (Rs.918.2mn at 1 Jan 2025 vs Rs.343.2mn at 1 Jan 2026 per the cash flow statement) that has since been drawn down, likely via a dividend or other capital distribution between the two periods not itemised as a 'Dividends Paid' cash flow line in either year shown here (both years' financing cash flows are Nil in this filing) -- flagged as a gap rather than guessed at.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for BOGA -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Additionally, the filing itself provides no 30/06/2025 balance-sheet comparative (only current quarter vs FYE 31/12/2025), so no YoY balance-sheet metrics could be computed from this document even though prior-year P&L figures were available -- only P&L-based YoY metrics are included in yoy_json. Net assets per share is disclosed as Rs.16.19 (2026) vs Rs.20.97 (2025) per Note 12.2, implying a large equity reduction (likely a dividend/distribution) between the two periods that is not identifiable from this filing's cash flow statement (financing activities show Nil for dividends paid in both years shown) -- left unexplained rather than guessed at.
interim_updates.takeaway: Strong headline growth (revenue +17.1%, PBT +52.8% YoY) is even better at the gross-margin level (48.3% vs 39.9%) but a sharp rise in the effective tax rate (47.7% vs 30.5% of PBT) consumed most of the extra pre-tax profit, so PAT grew only 14.9% and net margin was flat-to-down YoY -- investors focused on the PBT growth rate alone would overstate how much shareholders actually benefited this quarter.
operational_highlights: Revenue Rs.520.0mn, +17.1% YoY (Rs.443.9mn); gross profit Rs.251.1mn, +41.8% YoY, with gross margin expanding to 48.3% of revenue from 39.9%.
Profit from Operation Rs.165.7mn, +61.9% YoY (Rs.102.3mn); administrative expenses -6.7% to Rs.44.3mn.
Net exchange gain (within operating profit) fell to Rs.25.0mn from Rs.35.0mn a year earlier -28.6% YoY, a smaller currency tailwind than the prior-year quarter.
PBT Rs.168.4mn, +52.8% YoY (Rs.110.2mn), but income tax expense +139.2% YoY to Rs.80.3mn pushed the effective tax rate to 47.7% of PBT (from 30.5%), capping PAT growth at +14.9% to Rs.88.1mn.
Basic EPS Rs.0.93 vs Rs.0.81 prior year (+14.8%, tracking PAT growth).
Cash and cash equivalents Rs.508.2mn at 30/06/2026 (from Rs.343.2mn at FYE 31/12/2025); zero interest-bearing borrowings on the balance sheet; net operating cash flow Rs.211.2mn for the period.
key_drivers: Gross margin expansion (39.9% to 48.3% of revenue) is the primary driver of the earnings growth -- cost of sales grew only 2.2% while revenue grew 17.1%, implying favourable graphite pricing and/or cost control rather than pure volume growth.

Effective tax rate jumped to 47.7% of PBT from 30.5% (tax expense +139.2% YoY vs PBT +52.8% YoY) -- this single factor is why PAT growth (+14.9%) lagged PBT growth (+52.8%) so substantially; the filing gives no note explaining the tax-rate increase.

Net exchange gain (a P&L line within operating profit, tied to LKR/USD translation of monetary items per Note 7) fell 28.6% YoY to Rs.25.0mn from Rs.35.0mn, a smaller FX tailwind than the comparative quarter that partially offset the trading-margin improvement.

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
